scenario.prompt_to_agent:
IT and CS Dept users report they cannot reach Server Room
(1.0.0.x) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.x). But Other zone
(192.168.3.x) and Principle Room (192.168.4.x) CAN reach
those targets. router2 shows RIP routes intact and ip_forward
on. Identify what blocks IT/CS but not Other/Principle.

injection.action: add FORWARD DROP rules for IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24)
injection.command:
iptables -A FORWARD -s 192.168.1.0/24 -j DROP
  iptables -A FORWARD -s 192.168.2.0/24 -j DROP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 iptables FORWARD chain
Mechanism: New DROP rules block any forwarded packet whose
  source is in 192.168.1.0/24 (IT Dept) or 192.168.2.0/24
  (CS Dept). Office (192.168.3.x) and Principle (192.168.4.x)
  source addresses are not matched, so they are unaffected.
  Routing is healthy; the drop is at the firewall layer.
Localization: router2
Root cause: extraneous iptables FORWARD DROP rules for
  192.168.1.0/24 (IT) and 192.168.2.0/24 (CS)
Fix: `iptables -D FORWARD -s 192.168.1.0/23 -j DROP` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Router2’s host firewall (iptables), specifically the IPv4 FORWARD chain. 

Mechanism: Traffic from the IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) LANs must traverse router2 to reach the Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16). Router2 is enforcing two explicit DROP rules that match packets by source subnet in the FORWARD chain, so initial ICMP/TCP packets from IT/CS are discarded on arrival at router2 and never reach the destination LANs. Other and Principle zones are unaffected because their source subnets (192.168.3.0/24 and 192.168.4.0/24) are not matched by these DROP rules.

Localization: Router2, iptables FORWARD chain, affecting forwarding from the inter-router link (eth3/20.20.0.2) toward router2’s LAN interfaces (eth0: 1.0.0.1 and eth1: 128.168.0.1). Evidence: router2 iptables shows “-A FORWARD -s 192.168.1.0/24 -j DROP” and “-A FORWARD -s 192.168.2.0/24 -j DROP,” while router0/router1 have default ACCEPT. Pings from it_lab1/cs_lab1 to pc1/pc2 time out, but office_pc/pc0 can reach pc1/pc2, confirming selective blocking.

Root cause: Misconfigured firewall ACL on router2 that explicitly drops all forwarded traffic sourced from the IT and CS subnets.

Corrective fix: Remove or adjust the offending rules on router2 (e.g., delete the two DROP entries and replace with appropriate ACCEPT policies). Ensure persistence is updated (iptables-save/restore or FRR integration) so the fix survives reloads. Validate by retesting ping from IT/CS to 1.0.0.x and 128.168.0.x.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly identifies Router2 (iptables FORWARD chain) as the affected device.
The report explicitly names Router2's host firewall (iptables) and the IPv4 FORWARD chain as the affected component.
Agent explicitly identifies DROP rules matching source subnets 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24 in the FORWARD chain, recognizing the source-based filter pattern.
Recommends deleting the DROP rules on router2 (and persisting the change), which directly matches the expected remediation to remove the offending iptables drops.

The agent's log contains direct observations (selective ping failures, host IPs, and router2 iptables DROP rules) that support the diagnosis. The writeup's inferences follow logically from those observations with only a minor unsupported interface-detail claim.
